body:
Codex pre-review (not a collaborator review; no marker) @ 66df3e5b46865fb6a9ae077ec23c6eebb2833898

Verdict CLEAN

No findings. Trial merge with current upstream/main succeeded.

Tests: both new pins pass. Normal microarc_test_part passes 2/2. Quick gate passes: 143 post tests and 171 app tests across 46 suites. Clippy passes for camcraft-post, all targets, with warnings denied. Verification used RUSTC_WRAPPER=.

Mutation: made only the new loadedTool guard unconditional. Each pin independently fails: repeated tool gets two G30 blocks instead of one; return-tool sequence gets four M6 blocks instead of three. Restored the exact script; both pins pass again. Working tree is clean.

Extra safety case: microarc_test_part exercises consecutive same-tool sections at A-90 and A90 and checks that Z lifts before each rotary index. Both tests pass.

Policy checks pass. New unwrap/expect calls are confined to tests. The new Rust file has 81 lines; CPS is exempt from the size limit. The body explains all three removed golden lines and has Changelog: and Fixes #1626. No snapshot PNG, PROCESS_VERSION, Cargo dependency, .github or scripts changes.

Fixed the operator-stop finding from the latest review.

The post now resets loadedTool after emitted M0 and M1 stops, including setup changes and probe-result checks. The next section reloads the tool before G43, even when the number is unchanged. The decision file records why.

The four tormach_stop_tool pins cover program stop, optional stop, setup change, and probe check. Each checks M6 after the stop and before G43. Removing the after-operation reset makes its three pins fail. Removing the probe reset makes the probe pin fail. Restoring both passes all four pins and both existing same-tool pins.

Quick gate against upstream/main passed: 318 tests, 0 failed. Clippy for camcraft-post, all targets, passed with warnings denied.

New head: 439e77ee8967deb107a00ed4680ac6ea2fff3405.

Please re-review. The PR remains a draft.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 439e77ee8967deb107a00ed4680ac6ea2fff3405 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a SAFETY review. The change affects posted G-code.

Checks:
- The first tool change is always written. A repeated tool skips only the pre-change retract, G30 and M6. A different tool, or a return to an earlier tool, gets a tool change.
- G43, the machine-Z lift and clearance before the first X/Y move remain. Each section states the A axis again after a lift.
- The new head meets NeoTech's request on the old head. Both emitted operator-stop paths reset loadedTool. The next section loads its tool before G43. The decision file gives the reason and covers optional stops.
- No UI files changed. No screenshots are necessary. No dependencies, build scripts, workflows, process files or snapshot PNGs changed. The body has Changelog: and Fixes #1626. New expect calls are in tests only.

Golden check, line by line:
- docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc removes only G53 G0 Z0, G30 and T1 M6 before the second T1 section.
- The prior section ends with M9 and M5. G49 then G43 H1 remain. G53 G0 Z0 follows G43 before spindle start. Another G53 G0 Z0 remains before G0 A90. The cutting moves are unchanged.
- The T2 section still has its retract, G30 and M6. No other NC or CL golden changed. Both microarc_test_part tests pass.

Results, locally in .claude/worktrees/review-1741:
- Trial merge with upstream/main b8c0306a: no conflicts.
- cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main: PASS. Post: 147 passed in 21 suites. App: 171 passed in 26 suites. No failures or ignored tests.
- cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings: PASS.
- The first gate run used old cached test binaries with paths to a deleted worktree. They failed to find fixtures. I removed the post build outputs and ran the gate again with RUSTC_WRAPPER empty. All tests passed. These first failures are not code findings.

Mutations made by this reviewer, one at a time, then removed:
1. Remove the afterOp loadedTool reset: RED. The program-stop, optional-stop and setup-change tests fail at tormach_stop_tool.rs:24 (one M6 instead of two). The probe test passes.
2. Remove the probe-result loadedTool reset: RED. The probe test fails at the same assertion. The other three tests pass.
After restoration: GREEN, all four stop tests and both same-tool tests pass. git diff is empty.

Requested before merge: none.

No physical machine or PathPilot control was used. Windows, macOS, UI tests and the release gate were not run. No GitHub runner was used.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

@NeoTech: the new head 439e77e answers your operator-stop question. `loadedTool` is reset after each emitted `M0`/`M1`, so the next section always writes `T.. M6` again. Our review on this head cleared it. We leave the merge to you after you check it.
